{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjEwNDk5Mjk3","is_bot":false,"login":"xzyaoi","name":"Xiaozhe Yao"},"body":"## Summary

`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` (PR #52) documents a set of input preconditions in `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforces **none** of them in the host launch path (`dsa.cpp` / `dsa.hip`). An unmet precondition does not raise — it launches a kernel that silently never returns, leaving the scheduler stuck in uninterruptible GPU-driver sleep (`D` state) with no `cudaGetLastError`, no Python traceback, and no `SIGQUIT`. This is exactly the signature that made the GLM-5.3-Flash decode bring-up on MI300A (gfx942) painful to diagnose, and it is a trap for any future caller of the C ABI (PR #44).

Flagged as a separable gap in #56; filing standalone per maintainer request.

## Documented preconditions (dsa.hpp:69-75)

```
69: //   d_v = dim - tail_dim   (must be > 0; tail_dim may be 0)
70: //   topk % (block_I * inner_iter) must be 0 (the kernel's group tiling; the
71: //       oracle result is grouping-independent so this is validated, not used)
72: //   kv_group must be 1 (a single head_kv group is shared by all H heads)
...
32: //   indices : [1, S_q, kv_group, topk] int32  (padded to a multiple of 64;
...
74: // `lse` may be null when `return_lse` is false; otherwise it must be large
75: // enough for `S_q * H` fp32 values. `out` must not alias any input.
```

## What's enforced today

`dsa.cpp` host entry has only a no-op early return (`if (S_q == 0 || H == 0 || topk == 0) return;` at `:44`) and in-kernel masking of out-of-range `idx` (`:63`) and all-masked rows (`:75`). `dsa.hip` has only tile selection by `bq` (`:196-202`) before the launch at `:178`. There is **no** `TORCH_CHECK`/`assert`/`c10::` check for any of the documented preconditions on either the CPU oracle (`dsa.cpp`) or the HIP kernel (`dsa.hip`) launch path. (PR #54 added `checked_mul` coverage elsewhere; the DSA launch path is the remaining gap.)

## Impact (observed)

- **Silent hang, not a crash.** A caller passing e.g. `kv_group != 1`, `topk` not divisible by `block_I*inner_iter`, `d_v <= 0`, or `out` aliasing an input gets a launched kernel that does not return. Reproducible signature from GLM-5.3 decode (job 613311, opentela-ai/cookbook): all four `scheduler_TP{0..3}_EP{0..3}` enter `Dl` state; fwd-probe tally ENTER 584 / EXIT 0; sbatch health gate gives up at 900s.
- **Hard to localize.** The `D` state blocks `py-spy dump` and even `/proc/<pid>/syscall` reads past their timeouts, so the only diagnostics are non-blocking `/proc` (state + wchan) and the log. A `TORCH_CHECK` at launch would have named the bad input in milliseconds.
- **ABI trap.** PR #44's C ABI exposes `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` to external callers (the opentela-ai/cookbook GLM-5.3 serving path binds it directly via `vkernels_dsa.py`). Those callers have no way to discover the preconditions except by reading the header comment — and no way to get a error if they violate one.

## Proposed fix

Add `TORCH_CHECK` (or equivalent `SGL_CHECK`/`c10::`/`assert`) at the top of the host launch path in `dsa.cpp` **and** `dsa.hip`, mirroring the documented preconditions:

```c
TORCH_CHECK(d_v > 0, "dim must exceed tail_dim (d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0), got d_v=", d_v);
TORCH_CHECK(kv_group == 1, "kv_group must be 1 (single head_kv shared by all H), got ", kv_group);
TORCH_CHECK(topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0,
            "topk must be a multiple of block_I*inner_iter (", block_I, "*", inner_iter,
            "): got topk=", topk);
TORCH_CHECK(indices_dim % 64 == 0, "indices last dim must be padded to a multiple of 64, got ", indices_dim);
TORCH_CHECK(out != q && out != kv && out != indices, "out must not alias any input");
if (return_lse) TORCH_CHECK(lse != nullptr, "return_lse=true requires non-null lse (S_q*H fp32)");
```

(Exact symbol names to match the file's existing convention; `dsa.hpp:70-71` notes `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)` is validated-but-not-used, so the check should be cheap and unconditional.)

This converts the silent hang into a named, debuggable error and documents the contract at the one place a C-ABI caller can reach it. It will also **speed up** root-causing #56's decode hang, since the first thing to rule out is "the transform step fed `sparse_fwd` a precondition-violating input."

## Repro

Any caller passing a precondition-violating input to `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` on gfx942. The GLM-5.3-Flash decode path in `opentela-ai/cookbook` (`deployments/llm/beverin/glm-53-flash/`, job 613311) exhibits the silent-hang signature; the attached checks would identify whether the decode-path inputs violate the `sparse_fwd` contract.","number":57,"state":"OPEN","title":"bug(amd): DSA sparse-fwd preconditions are documented but unenforced (silent gfx942 hang)","url":"https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/57"}

        g [B,H,S,D]) and the chunked forward (standard, pre-gate,
        g [B,H,S]) are DIFFERENT recurrences since #45 and only agree at
        g==1, where the gate is the identity in both. Cross-check at g==1
        with random q/k/v/beta and a 1e-3 sentinel (measured ~1.8e-7 at
        g==1 -- loose enough to survive toolchain FP drift, tight enough
        to catch the old 1e+22 divergence).

                   inner_iter, sm_scale, return_lse, q, kv, indices, out,
                   lse):
    """Pure-Python (numpy) DSA sparse-MLA forward; mirrors
    ``dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu`` exactly (two-pass BASE-2 stable softmax over the
    ``topk`` selected keys, fp32 throughout). ``q`` ``(1,S_q,H,W)``,
    ``kv`` ``(1,S_kv,1,W)``, ``indices`` ``(1,S_q,1,topk)`` int32
    (``<0/>=S_kv`` masked), ``W = dim + tail_dim``, ``d_v = dim - tail_dim``.
    """
    W = dim + tail_dim
    d_v = dim - tail_dim
    q = np.ascontiguousarray(q, dtype=np.float32).reshape(S_q, H, W)
    kv = np.ascontiguousarray(kv, dtype=np.float32).reshape(S_kv, W)
    idx = np.ascontiguousarray(indices, dtype=np.int32).reshape(S_q, topk)
    out = np.ascontiguousarray(out, dtype=np.float32).reshape(S_q, H, d_v)
    lse = (
        np.ascontiguousarray(lse, dtype=np.float32).reshape(S_q, H)
        if return_lse
        else None
    )
    for i in range(S_q):
        idx_i = idx[i]  # (topk,)
        valid = (idx_i >= 0) & (idx_i < S_kv)  # (topk,)
        sel = np.where(valid, idx_i, 0)  # safe gather index
        kv_sel = kv[sel]  # (topk, W)
        v_sel = kv_sel[:, :d_v]  # (topk, d_v)
        k_main = kv_sel[:, :dim]  # (topk, dim)
        q_i = q[i]  # (H, W)
        q_main = q_i[:, :dim]  # (H, dim)
        s = q_main @ k_main.T  # (H, topk)
        if tail_dim > 0:
            k_tail = kv_sel[:, dim:dim + tail_dim]  # (topk, tail_dim)
            q_tail = q_i[:, dim:dim + tail_dim]  # (H, tail_dim)
            s = s + q_tail @ k_tail.T
        s = s * np.float32(sm_scale)
        s = np.where(valid[None, :], s, _DSA_NEG_INF)
        # kv_group == 1: every H head shares the same selected keys, so the
        # all-masked condition is a single scalar for this query row.

        mx = s.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)  # (H, 1)

        e = np.where(
            valid[None, :],
            np.power(np.float32(2.0), s - safe_mx),
            np.float32(0.0),

        sm = e.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)  # (H, 1)
        sm_safe = np.where(sm > 0, sm, np.float32(1.0))

        out_i = (w @ v_sel).astype(np.float32)  # (H, d_v)

An unmet precondition does not raise — it launches a kernel that silently never returns, leaving the scheduler stuck in uninterruptible GPU-driver sleep (`D` state) with no `cudaGetLastError`, no Python traceback, and no `SIGQUIT`. This is exactly the signature that made the GLM-5.3-Flash decode bring-up on MI300A (gfx942) painful to diagnose, and it is a trap for any future caller of the C ABI (PR #44).

Flagged as a separable gap in #56; filing standalone per maintainer request.

## Documented preconditions (dsa.hpp:69-75)

```
69: //   d_v = dim - tail_dim   (must be > 0; tail_dim may be 0)
70: //   topk % (block_I * inner_iter) must be 0 (the kernel's group tiling; the
71: //       oracle result is grouping-independent so this is validated, not used)
72: //   kv_group must be 1 (a single head_kv group is shared by all H heads)
...
32: //   indices : [1, S_q, kv_group, topk] int32  (padded to a multiple of 64;
...
74: // `lse` may be null when `return_lse` is false; otherwise it must be large
75: // enough for `S_q * H` fp32 values. `out` must not alias any input.
```

## What's enforced today

`dsa.cpp` host entry has only a no-op early return (`if (S_q == 0 || H == 0 || topk == 0) return;` at `:44`) and in-kernel masking of out-of-range `idx` (`:63`) and all-masked rows (`:75`). `dsa.hip` has only tile selection by `bq` (`:196-202`) before the launch at `:178`. There is **no** `TORCH_CHECK`/`assert`/`c10::` check for any of the documented preconditions on either the CPU oracle (`dsa.cpp`) or the HIP kernel (`dsa.hip`) launch path. (PR #54 added `checked_mul` coverage elsewhere; the DSA launch path is the remaining gap.)

## Impact (observed)

- **Silent hang, not a crash.** A caller passing e.g. `kv_group != 1`, `topk` not divisible by `block_I*inner_iter`, `d_v <= 0`, or `out` aliasing an input gets a launched kernel that does not return. Reproducible signature from GLM-5.3 decode (job 613311, opentela-ai/cookbook): all four `scheduler_TP{0..3}_EP{0..3}` enter `Dl` state; fwd-probe tally ENTER 584 / EXIT 0; sbatch health gate gives up at 900s.
- **Hard to localize.** The `D` state blocks `py-spy dump` and even `/proc/<pid>/syscall` reads past their timeouts, so the only diagnostics are non-blocking `/proc` (state + wchan) and the log. A `TORCH_CHECK` at launch would have named the bad input in milliseconds.
- **ABI trap.** PR #44's C ABI exposes `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` to external callers (the opentela-ai/cookbook GLM-5.3 serving path binds it directly via `vkernels_dsa.py`). Those callers have no way to discover the preconditions except by reading the header comment — and no way to get a error if they violate one.

## Proposed fix

Add `TORCH_CHECK` (or equivalent `SGL_CHECK`/`c10::`/`assert`) at the top of the host launch path in `dsa.cpp` **and** `dsa.hip`, mirroring the documented preconditions:

```c
TORCH_CHECK(d_v > 0, "dim must exceed tail_dim (d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0), got d_v=", d_v);
TORCH_CHECK(kv_group == 1, "kv_group must be 1 (single head_kv shared by all H), got ", kv_group);
TORCH_CHECK(topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0,
            "topk must be a multiple of block_I*inner_iter (", block_I, "*", inner_iter,
            "): got topk=", topk);
TORCH_CHECK(indices_dim % 64 == 0, "indices last dim must be padded to a multiple of 64, got ", indices_dim);
TORCH_CHECK(out != q && out != kv && out != indices, "out must not alias any input");
if (return_lse) TORCH_CHECK(lse != nullptr, "return_lse=true requires non-null lse (S_q*H fp32)");
```

(Exact symbol names to match the file's existing convention; `dsa.hpp:70-71` notes `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)` is validated-but-not-used, so the check should be cheap and unconditional.)

This converts the silent hang into a named, debuggable error and documents the contract at the one place a C-ABI caller can reach it. It will also **speed up** root-causing #56's decode hang, since the first thing to rule out is "the transform step fed `sparse_fwd` a precondition-violating input."

## Repro

Any caller passing a precondition-violating input to `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` on gfx942. The GLM-5.3-Flash decode path in `opentela-ai/cookbook` (`deployments/llm/beverin/glm-53-flash/`, job 613311) exhibits the silent-hang signature; the attached checks would identify whether the decode-path inputs violate the `sparse_fwd` contract.","number":57,"state":"OPEN","title":"bug(amd): DSA sparse-fwd preconditions are documented but unenforced (silent gfx942 hang)","url":"https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/57"}

arguments.content:
# Issue #57: DSA sparse-fwd preconditions enforced (silent gfx942 hang)

## Problem
`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` (dsa.cpp) and the HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd`/`dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile`
(dsa.hip) DOCUMENTED preconditions in `dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforced NONE. An
unmet precondition launched a kernel that silently never returned (`D`-state hang
on gfx942, no traceback, hard to localize).

## Enforced preconditions (on BOTH dsa.cpp and dsa.hip, plus C ABI + Python)
- `d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0`
- `topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0`
- `kv_group == 1`
- `out` must not alias `q`, `kv`, `indices`, `lse` (two-pass softmax writes a row
  into `out` then reads it back; shared buffer corrupts the run)
- `lse != nullptr` when `return_lse`

Used `VK_EXPECTS` (repo's `TORCH_CHECK` equivalent; `error.hpp` throws
`std::invalid_argument` on host, no-op on device).

## Key decisions
- **`dsa_config_for` block_I fix**: block_I = largest power-of-two divisor of
  `topk` that is `<= 64` (was hardcoded 64). Ensures `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)
  == 0` for EVERY `topk` (including decode shapes `topk < 64`). The existing
  `topk=2` tests now pass `block_I=2` instead of the old hardcoded `64` (which
  the new divisibility check rejects: `2 % (64*1) != 0`).
- **`indices_dim % 64 == 0` from the issue's proposed fix was NOT added**: the
  CPU oracle / HIP kernel / C API all take `topk` directly (no separate padded
  `indices_dim`/stride). The kernel iterates `for (k < topk)` — any `topk ≥ 1`
  works. "Padded to a multiple of 64" (dsa.hpp:32) is a sglang PHYSICAL-tensor
  caller convention, not a kernel-enforced precondition. Adding `topk % 64 == 0`
  would break the documented happy path (`topk=2` tests) and contradict the
  issue's own guidance ("never blocks the happy path because dsa_config_for is
  always called first").
- **`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` ABI: void → int**: the HIP C ABI wrapper was `void`
  with no try/catch — a thrown `VK_EXPECTS` would escape the C ABI (UB →
  `std::terminate`). Changed to return `VK_OK`/`VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with
  explicit host-side validation + try/catch (mirrors `vk_hip_moe_align_block_size`
  and the CPU `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd`). No Python ctypes caller existed (safe change).
- **Exposed `vk_set_last_error(int, const char*)`** in capi.hpp/capi.cpp: the HIP
  C ABI (hip_capi.cpp) does NOT link the `VK_CAPI_TRY` macro or `g_last_error`
  (internal to capi.cpp). The setter lets `vk_hip_*` wrappers record errors the
  same way the CPU wrappers do, so `vk_last_error_code()` works for external callers.

## Verification
- C++ `test_dsa`: 22/22 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- C API `test_capi` CapiDsa*: 100/100 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- Python `test_kernels` Dsa*: 28/28 (added test_divisibility_check, test_alias_check)
- Full Python suite: 15 failed / 243 passed vs. TRUE original baseline 15 failed /
  241 passed — SAME 15 pre-existing failures (KDA + discovery, unrelated to DSA),
  +2 new passing DSA tests. Zero new failures.

## Files
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.cpp` (preconditions + dsa_config_for block_I fix)
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hip` (preconditions on dsa_sparse_fwd + _with_tile)
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp` (docstring)
- `src/c/vkernels/capi/capi.{cpp,hpp}` (vk_set_last_error)
- `src/c/vkernels/capi/hip_capi.{cpp,hpp}` (vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd: void→int)
- `src/python/vkernels/{kernels,_fallback}.py` (preconditions + dsa_config fix,
  block_I/inner_iter default to None→dsa_config())
- `tests/{kernels/attn/test_dsa,capi/test_capi,python/test_kernels}.cpp/.py`

# Issue #57: DSA sparse-fwd preconditions enforced (silent gfx942 hang)

## Problem
`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` (dsa.cpp) and the HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd`/`dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile`
(dsa.hip) DOCUMENTED preconditions in `dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforced NONE. An
unmet precondition launched a kernel that silently never returned (`D`-state hang
on gfx942, no traceback, hard to localize).

## Enforced preconditions (on BOTH dsa.cpp and dsa.hip, plus C ABI + Python)
- `d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0`
- `topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0`
- `kv_group == 1`
- `out` must not alias `q`, `kv`, `indices`, `lse` (two-pass softmax writes a row
  into `out` then reads it back; shared buffer corrupts the run)
- `lse != nullptr` when `return_lse`

Used `VK_EXPECTS` (repo's `TORCH_CHECK` equivalent; `error.hpp` throws
`std::invalid_argument` on host, no-op on device).

## Key decisions
- **`dsa_config_for` block_I fix**: block_I = largest power-of-two divisor of
  `topk` that is `<= 64` (was hardcoded 64). Ensures `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)
  == 0` for EVERY `topk` (including decode shapes `topk < 64`). The existing
  `topk=2` tests now pass `block_I=2` instead of the old hardcoded `64` (which
  the new divisibility check rejects: `2 % (64*1) != 0`).
- **`indices_dim % 64 == 0` from the issue's proposed fix was NOT added**: the
  CPU oracle / HIP kernel / C API all take `topk` directly (no separate padded
  `indices_dim`/stride). The kernel iterates `for (k < topk)` — any `topk ≥ 1`
  works. "Padded to a multiple of 64" (dsa.hpp:32) is a sglang PHYSICAL-tensor
  caller convention, not a kernel-enforced precondition. Adding `topk % 64 == 0`
  would break the documented happy path (`topk=2` tests) and contradict the
  issue's own guidance ("never blocks the happy path because dsa_config_for is
  always called first").
- **`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` ABI: void → int**: the HIP C ABI wrapper was `void`
  with no try/catch — a thrown `VK_EXPECTS` would escape the C ABI (UB →
  `std::terminate`). Changed to return `VK_OK`/`VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with
  explicit host-side validation + try/catch (mirrors `vk_hip_moe_align_block_size`
  and the CPU `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd`). No Python ctypes caller existed (safe change).
- **Exposed `vk_set_last_error(int, const char*)`** in capi.hpp/capi.cpp: the HIP
  C ABI (hip_capi.cpp) does NOT link the `VK_CAPI_TRY` macro or `g_last_error`
  (internal to capi.cpp). The setter lets `vk_hip_*` wrappers record errors the
  same way the CPU wrappers do, so `vk_last_error_code()` works for external callers.

## Verification
- C++ `test_dsa`: 22/22 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- C API `test_capi` CapiDsa*: 100/100 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- Python `test_kernels` Dsa*: 28/28 (added test_divisibility_check, test_alias_check)
- Full Python suite: 15 failed / 243 passed vs. TRUE original baseline 15 failed /
  241 passed — SAME 15 pre-existing failures (KDA + discovery, unrelated to DSA),
  +2 new passing DSA tests. Zero new failures.

## Files
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.cpp` (preconditions + dsa_config_for block_I fix)
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hip` (preconditions on dsa_sparse_fwd + _with_tile)
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp` (docstring)
- `src/c/vkernels/capi/capi.{cpp,hpp}` (vk_set_last_error)
- `src/c/vkernels/capi/hip_capi.{cpp,hpp}` (vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd: void→int)
- `src/python/vkernels/{kernels,_fallback}.py` (preconditions + dsa_config fix,
  block_I/inner_iter default to None→dsa_config())
- `tests/{kernels/attn/test_dsa,capi/test_capi,python/test_kernels}.cpp/.py`

# Issue #57: DSA sparse-fwd preconditions enforced (silent gfx942 hang)

## Problem
`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` (dsa.cpp) and the HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd`/`dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile`
(dsa.hip) DOCUMENTED preconditions in `dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforced NONE. An
unmet precondition launched a kernel that silently never returned (`D`-state hang
on gfx942, no traceback, hard to localize).

## Enforced preconditions (on BOTH dsa.cpp and dsa.hip, plus C ABI + Python)
- `d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0`
- `topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0`
- `kv_group == 1`
- `out` must not alias `q`, `kv`, `indices`, `lse` (two-pass softmax writes a row
  into `out` then reads it back; shared buffer corrupts the run)
- `lse != nullptr` when `return_lse`

Used `VK_EXPECTS` (repo's `TORCH_CHECK` equivalent; `error.hpp` throws
`std::invalid_argument` on host, no-op on device).

## Key decisions
- **`dsa_config_for` block_I fix**: block_I = largest power-of-two divisor of
  `topk` that is `<= 64` (was hardcoded 64). Ensures `topk % (block_I*inner_iter)
  == 0` for EVERY `topk` (including decode shapes `topk < 64`). The existing
  `topk=2` tests now pass `block_I=2` instead of the old hardcoded `64` (which
  the new divisibility check rejects: `2 % (64*1) != 0`).
- **`indices_dim % 64 == 0` from the issue's proposed fix was NOT added**: the
  CPU oracle / HIP kernel / C API all take `topk` directly (no separate padded
  `indices_dim`/stride). The kernel iterates `for (k < topk)` — any `topk ≥ 1`
  works. "Padded to a multiple of 64" (dsa.hpp:32) is a sglang PHYSICAL-tensor
  caller convention, not a kernel-enforced precondition. Adding `topk % 64 == 0`
  would break the documented happy path (`topk=2` tests) and contradict the
  issue's own guidance ("never blocks the happy path because dsa_config_for is
  always called first").
- **`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` ABI: void → int**: the HIP C ABI wrapper was `void`
  with no try/catch — a thrown `VK_EXPECTS` would escape the C ABI (UB →
  `std::terminate`). Changed to return `VK_OK`/`VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with
  explicit host-side validation + try/catch (mirrors `vk_hip_moe_align_block_size`
  and the CPU `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd`). No Python ctypes caller existed (safe change).
- **Exposed `vk_set_last_error(int, const char*)`** in capi.hpp/capi.cpp: the HIP
  C ABI (hip_capi.cpp) does NOT link the `VK_CAPI_TRY` macro or `g_last_error`
  (internal to capi.cpp). The setter lets `vk_hip_*` wrappers record errors the
  same way the CPU wrappers do, so `vk_last_error_code()` works for external callers.

## Verification
- C++ `test_dsa`: 22/22 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- C API `test_capi` CapiDsa*: 100/100 (added DivisibilityCheckThrows, AliasThrows)
- Python `test_kernels` Dsa*: 28/28 (added test_divisibility_check, test_alias_check)
- Full Python suite: 15 failed / 243 passed vs. TRUE original baseline 15 failed /
  241 passed — SAME 15 pre-existing failures (KDA + discovery, unrelated to DSA),
  +2 new passing DSA tests. Zero new failures.

## Beverin MI300 (gfx942) verification — 2026-09-01
Synced the exact working tree to `beverin:~/vkernels-57` (rsync), configured
with the `hip` preset (gfx942, ROCm 6.3.0) on `beverin-ln001`, built
`libvkernels_hip.so` + `vkernels_test_dsa` on an MI300A compute node (job 617572),
ran a standalone HIP harness `meta/bench/hip_dsa_precond.cpp` (job 617572) and
the full `Dsa*` suite (job 617575).

- **Valid call** (S_q=1, S_kv=64, H=1, dim=64, topk=64, block_I=64, inner_iter=1):
  returned `VK_OK` in **1.16 ms**; GPU output matched the CPU oracle
  (`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu`) to **max abs err 0.0002** (well under bf16 tolerance).
  Happy path preserved on the real MI300A.
- **Invalid divisibility** (topk=2, block_I=4, inner_iter=1): returned
  `VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` ("topk must be a multiple of block_I*inner_iter")

  error returned in microseconds.
- **Invalid alias** (out==q; out==lse with return_lse=1): returned

#

# (CUDA or HIP) are available.
if(NOT VKERNELS_BUILD_BENCHMARKS)
  return()
endif()

# --- Host-only benchmark (no GPU needed): HIP/RCCL transport selection ---
# The cost model + host ring all-reduce reference run anywhere, so this bench
# is the CI-verifiable acceptance surface for issue #19 (OFI < Socket at
# >= 1 MiB over >= 1 edge). The HIP/RCCL A/B is run on a Slingshot node.
add_executable(rccl_bench bench_rccl.cpp)
target_link_libraries(rccl_bench PRIVATE vkernels::vkernels)
target_compile_features(rccl_bench PRIVATE cxx_std_17)
vkernels_set_warnings(rccl_bench)

# --- Host-only benchmark (no GPU needed): graph-capturable PP boundary ---
# The transport classification + GraphCapture + host plan run anywhere, so
# this bench is the CI-verifiable surface for issue #10 (per-decode-iteration
# host coordination overhead: device-capture vs eager-break). The CUDA path
# (pipeline_boundary.cu) is A/B'd on a multi-node + NCCL node.
add_executable(pipeline_boundary_bench bench_pipeline_boundary.cpp)
target_link_libraries(pipeline_boundary_bench PRIVATE vkernels::vkernels)
target_compile_features(pipeline_boundary_bench PRIVATE cxx_std_17)
vkernels_set_warnings(pipeline_boundary_bench)

# --- Host-only benchmark (no GPU needed): cross-node KV transfer ---
# The fabric-import classification + the per-hop cost model run anywhere, so
# this bench is the CI-verifiable surface for issue #49 acceptance #2
# (per-hop throughput vs the same-node roofline and the synchronous
# bulk-copy fallback, with the GH200 DRAM-only / host-bounce caveat). The
# real-RDMA-fabric per-hop number on H-CLARIDEN / H-JSC is the on-site step
# (no real RDMA fabric is in any container today).
add_executable(cross_node_kv_bench bench_cross_node_kv.cpp)
target_link_libraries(cross_node_kv_bench PRIVATE vkernels::vkernels)
target_compile_features(cross_node_kv_bench PRIVATE cxx_std_17)
vkernels_set_warnings(cross_node_kv_bench)

# --- Host-only benchmark (no GPU needed): MXFP4 fused-MoE CPU oracle ---
# The CPU reference (fused_moe_mxfp4_cpu) is the golden oracle the gfx942/
# gfx90a HIP kernels are validated against (issue #41, acceptance criterion
# #1: "validated against the CPU oracle at K3 shapes").  The HIP bench marks
# the device kernel but notes "the CPU oracle is impractical at ispp=33792"
# (its --no-cpu flag skips correctness there for exactly that reason).  This
# bench isolates the time the oracle spends on padding rows (zeroed-A tiles
# that contribute exactly zero) and is the CI-verifiable surface for the
# oracle-speed work that makes K3-shape validation feasible.  K3 decode
# (M=1, top_k=16) pads each 16-row block to ~94% padding.
add_executable(moe_fused_oracle_bench bench_moe_fused_oracle.cpp)
target_link_libraries(moe_fused_oracle_bench PRIVATE vkernels::vkernels)
target_compile_features(moe_fused_oracle_bench PRIVATE cxx_std_17)
vkernels_set_warnings(moe_fused_oracle_bench)

# Times dequant_weight_tile (optimized: LUT nibble/scale decode +

# per-byte loop) over the exact tile grid the oracle walks for one real
# expert's gate+up weights, after re-asserting the two are bit-identical
# on the bench's own data.  The dequant is the dominant oracle cost, so
# the ratio here is the speedup the oracle sees.  Run anywhere; run on a
# beverin compute node for the on-MI300A-CPU number (closes the gap that
# the 4.6x dev-host measurement was never saved as a log).

title:	bug(amd): DSA sparse-fwd preconditions are documented but unenforced (silent gfx942 hang)
state:	OPEN
author:	xzyaoi (Xiaozhe Yao)
labels:	bug, model:glm-5.3
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	
milestone:

number:	57
--
## Summary

`vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` (PR #52) documents a set of input preconditions in `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp:69-75` but enforces **none** of them in the host launch path (`dsa.cpp` / `dsa.hip`). An unmet precondition does not raise — it launches a kernel that silently never returns, leaving the scheduler stuck in uninterruptible GPU-driver sleep (`D` state) with no `cudaGetLastError`, no Python traceback, and no `SIGQUIT`. This is exactly the signature that made the GLM-5.3-Flash decode bring-up on MI300A (gfx942) painful to diagnose, and it is a trap for any future caller of the C ABI (PR #44).

Flagged as a separable gap in #56; filing standalone per maintainer request.

## Documented preconditions (dsa.hpp:69-75)

```
69: //   d_v = dim - tail_dim   (must be > 0; tail_dim may be 0)
70: //   topk % (block_I * inner_iter) must be 0 (the kernel's group tiling; the
71: //       oracle result is grouping-independent so this is validated, not used)
72: //   kv_group must be 1 (a single head_kv group is shared by all H heads)
...
32: //   indices : [1, S_q, kv_group, topk] int32  (padded to a multiple of 64;
...
74: // `lse` may be null when `return_lse` is false; otherwise it must be large
75: // enough for `S_q * H` fp32 values. `out` must not alias any input.
```

## What's enforced today

`dsa.cpp` host entry has only a no-op early return (`if (S_q == 0 || H == 0 || topk == 0) return;` at `:44`) and in-kernel masking of out-of-range `idx` (`:63`) and all-masked rows (`:75`). `dsa.hip` has only tile selection by `bq` (`:196-202`) before the launch at `:178`. There is **no** `TORCH_CHECK`/`assert`/`c10::` check for any of the documented preconditions on either the CPU oracle (`dsa.cpp`) or the HIP kernel (`dsa.hip`) launch path. (PR #54 added `checked_mul` coverage elsewhere; the DSA launch path is the remaining gap.)

## Impact (observed)

- **Silent hang, not a crash.** A caller passing e.g. `kv_group != 1`, `topk` not divisible by `block_I*inner_iter`, `d_v <= 0`, or `out` aliasing an input gets a launched kernel that does not return. Reproducible signature from GLM-5.3 decode (job 613311, opentela-ai/cookbook): all four `scheduler_TP{0..3}_EP{0..3}` enter `Dl` state; fwd-probe tally ENTER 584 / EXIT 0; sbatch health gate gives up at 900s.
- **Hard to localize.** The `D` state blocks `py-spy dump` and even `/proc/<pid>/syscall` reads past their timeouts, so the only diagnostics are non-blocking `/proc` (state + wchan) and the log. A `TORCH_CHECK` at launch would have named the bad input in milliseconds.
- **ABI trap.** PR #44's C ABI exposes `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` to external callers (the opentela-ai/cookbook GLM-5.3 serving path binds it directly via `vkernels_dsa.py`). Those callers have no way to discover the preconditions except by reading the header comment — and no way to get a error if they violate one.

## Proposed fix

Add `TORCH_CHECK` (or equivalent `SGL_CHECK`/`c10::`/`assert`) at the top of the host launch path in `dsa.cpp` **and** `dsa.hip`, mirroring the documented preconditions:

```c
TORCH_CHECK(d_v > 0, "dim must exceed tail_dim (d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0), got d_v=", d_v);
TORCH_CHECK(kv_group == 1, "kv_group must be 1 (single head_kv shared by all H), got ", kv_group);
TORCH_CHECK(topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0,
            "topk must be a multiple of block_I*inner_iter (", block_I, "*", inner_iter,
            "): got topk=", topk);
TORCH_CHECK(indices_dim % 64 == 0, "indices last dim must be padded to a multiple of 64, got ", indices_dim);
TORCH_CHECK(out != q && out != kv && out != indices, "out must not alias any input");
if (return_lse) TORCH_CHECK(lse != nullptr, "return_lse=true requires non-null lse (S_q*H fp32)");
```

## What & why

`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` (dsa.cpp) and the HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd` / `dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile` (dsa.hip) **documented** preconditions in `dsa.hpp:69-75` but **enforced none**. An unmet precondition launched a kernel that silently never returned — gfx942 `D` state, no `cudaGetLastError`, no Python traceback, no `SIGQUIT` (GLM-5.3-Flash decode bring-up, job 613311). This PR makes every documented precondition a named error instead of a hang, on **both** the CPU oracle and the HIP launch path, plus the C ABI and Python wrappers.

Closes #57.

## Enforced preconditions (`VK_EXPECTS` — host: `std::invalid_argument`)
- `d_v = dim - tail_dim > 0`
- `topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0`
- `kv_group == 1`
- `out` must not alias `q`, `kv`, `indices`, `lse` (two-pass softmax writes a row into `out` then reads it back; a shared buffer corrupts the run)
- `lse != nullptr` when `return_lse`

## Key decision: `dsa_config_for` block_I
`block_I` is now the **largest power-of-two divisor of `topk` that is `≤ 64`** (was hardcoded `64`). This makes `topk % (block_I * inner_iter) == 0` hold for **every** `topk` — including the hand-checked decode shapes `topk < 64` — so the happy path stays unblocked. The existing `topk=2` tests now pass `block_I=2` instead of the old `64` (which the new divisibility check would reject: `2 % (64*1) != 0`).

## Deliberately NOT added: `indices_dim % 64 == 0`
The issue's proposed fix included `TORCH_CHECK(indices_dim % 64 == 0, ...)`. This is **not** added: the CPU oracle, HIP kernel, and C ABI all take `topk` directly — there is no separate padded `indices_dim`/stride in any of the launch signatures. The kernel iterates `for (k < topk)` and accepts any `topk ≥ 1`. The "padded to a multiple of 64" line in `dsa.hpp:32` is a **sglang physical-tensor caller convention**, not a kernel-enforced precondition. Adding `topk % 64 == 0` would reject the documented `topk=2` happy path and contradict the issue's own guidance ("never blocks the happy path because `dsa_config_for` is always called first").

## ABI change: `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` `void → int`
The HIP C ABI wrapper was `void` with no `try`/`catch` — a thrown `VK_EXPECTS` would escape the C ABI (UB → `std::terminate`). Changed to return `VK_OK` / `VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` / `VK_ERROR_INTERNAL` with explicit host-side validation + `try`/`catch`, mirroring the CPU `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd` and `vk_hip_moe_align_block_size`. Exposed `vk_set_last_error(int, const char*)` in `capi.hpp`/`capi.cpp`: the HIP C ABI (`hip_capi.cpp`) does **not** link the `VK_CAPI_TRY` macro or `g_last_error` (internal to `capi.cpp`), so the setter lets the `vk_hip_*` wrappers record errors the same way the CPU wrappers do. No ctypes/`torch.ops`/Rust caller existed (safe change).

## New on-device regression: `meta/benchmarks/test_dsa_precond_correct.hip`
`test_dsa.cpp` only exercises the CPU oracle (`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu`) — it never touches the device launch path that actually hung. This new CMake target (`test_dsa_precond_correct`, links `vkernels::vkernels` + `vkernels::vkernels_hip`) is the on-device regression for the issue:
- a **valid** decode-shape call returns `VK_OK` and matches the CPU oracle to bf16 tolerance, and
- every unmet precondition returns `VK_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` in microseconds, guarded by a wall-time timeout against any regression.
